1.explanation:
1. We set the page background color to #f4f4f4 to simulate the "grey on grey" scenario described in the bug report.  
2. We render the standard Carbon OverflowMenu (v10) with four items.  
3. When you click the kebab (vertical ellipsis) button, the dropdown panel that appears is also light grey, matching the page background.  
4. This reproduces the low-contrast bug: without a "light" modifier (e.g. `--light`), the menu panel cannot be styled to a contrasting white and fails on grey backgrounds.  

You can confirm that adding a hypothetical `light` modifier (for example, customizing the CSS on `.my-custom-menu --light`) would fix the contrast, but that modifier is not currently implemented in the component.
1.bug_scenario: In the repro above we place the default OverflowMenu on a grey page background (`#f4f4f4`). When you open the menu, the dropdown panel itself also uses a light-grey background, almost the same shade as the page. As a result the menu panel "blends" into the page and you lose the visual separation between menu and page content.
